description.text: Giovanni Gaetano Orsini, later Pope Nicholas III, was born around 1225 in Rome as the eldest son of Matteo Rosso Orsini, a powerful Roman nobleman.  He entered the Church and served under eight popes, becoming a cardinal‑deacon in 1244, protector of the Franciscans, and inquisitor‑general before being elected pope in a conclave that began in September 1277 and ended on 25 November 1277.

As pope, Nicholas III strengthened the papal position in Italy, negotiated a concordat with Rudolf I of Habsburg, and issued a constitution that forbade foreigners from holding civil office in Rome.  He focused on the Franciscan order, issuing the bull *Exiit qui seminat* in 1279, and was notorious for elevating close relatives to the cardinalate—an act of nepotism that drew criticism from contemporaries and from Dante, who condemned him in the *Inferno*.  He died suddenly on 22 August 1280 at his country retreat in Castro Soriano.

curiosities.text: Nicholas III was a cardinal for over three decades before becoming pope, having been created a cardinal‑deacon by Pope Innocent IV in 1244.
He was condemned by Dante Alighieri in the *Inferno* to the Third Bolgia of the Eighth Circle of Hell for simony, the practice of buying ecclesiastical offices.

During his papacy he elevated three of his close relatives to the cardinalate, a practice that earned him the nickname “little bears” (orsetti) in contemporary cartoons and was later lampooned by Dante.
